critical_concepts.elaboration: Executing large number of orders at extremely high speeds.
Implementing strict bounds to prevent runaway AI trades.

interactive_questions.title: Case 1: AI Trading Agent Cascades
interactive_questions.prompt: Observe multiple AI trading agents operating in an unregulated sandbox environment.
interactive_questions.question: What happens when multiple agents with similar reinforcement learning policies react to a slight market dip?
options: A. They naturally balance the market by taking opposing sides of trades.
B. They create a rapid feedback loop of selling, causing a flash crash.
C. They temporarily pause trading to wait for human intervention.
interactive_questions.answer: B. They create a rapid feedback loop of selling, causing a flash crash.
interactive_questions.explanation: If agents are trained on similar datasets or use identical strategies, they often exhibit herd behavior. In a downward trend, they all sell simultaneously, draining liquidity and crashing the price instantly.

theory.title: Algorithmic Herd Behavior
theory.content: Flash crashes occur when high-frequency trading algorithms all decide to sell a security at the same time, often triggered by minor news or price movements. This herd behavior creates a sudden vacuum of liquidity.
theory.analogy: A crowded theater where someone yells 'Fire!' and everyone rushes the single exit at once.
theory.application: Implement circuit breakers and position limits in algorithmic trading systems to prevent catastrophic feedback loops.
theory.critical_failure_vector: Correlated automated trading strategies can trigger devastating flash crashes by simultaneously reacting to the same market signals.
